entries.topic: Seasteading, charter cities, Pronomos, Praxis, network state (2008-2026)

claims.text: French Polynesia's governing Tapura Huiraatira party said its deal with the Seasteading Institute for a floating platform in the Atimaono lagoon 'was not a legal document' and expired at the end of 2017; opposition politician Valentina Cross had asked the government to withdraw

Romer began presenting charter cities in 2009; Honduras's Congress passed a RED constitutional amendment 124-1 in January 2011; the Supreme Court ruled REDs unconstitutional on 18 October 2012; Romer resigned from the transparency commission after learning from a newspaper of a September 2012 RED contract
Juan Orlando Hernández, as Congress president, announced the ZEDE law in early 2013; ZEDE land to be bought from owners rather than granted by the state

Patri Friedman incorporated Pronomos Capital in August 2019; Thiel was the anchor investor and supplied more than half of about $9 million raised; other seed backers named: Andreessen, Roger Ver, Balaji Srinivasan; Brimen working informally with Friedman on a Honduras project
Pronomos had raised at least $13.3 million by December 2023 from investors including Thiel and Andreessen; projects in the Mediterranean, Honduras and Nigeria

Pronomos financed Praxis; Thiel backs Pronomos; Michael Gibson, formerly of the Thiel Foundation, advises Pronomos; Dryden Brown posted in November 2024 'I went to Greenland to try to buy it'; Praxis account answered Trump's Greenland post 'According to plan'; Danish MP Rasmus Jarlov: no way Denmark would approve independence so Greenland could be bought

Praxis announced $525 million on 15 October 2024, primarily a drawdown facility (Arch Lending, GEM Digital, Manifold Trading); earlier backers Paradigm, Alameda Research, Three Arrows; location undetermined

Praxis signed a mostly non-binding MoU with +Colonia (Colonia del Sacramento, Uruguay) in 2026; developer Eduardo Bastitta, a former member of Milei's advisory council, cites about $1 billion of planned Praxis spending; Bastitta rules out a separate legal order; Milei walked the site in August 2023

Network School opened in Forest City, Johor, on 23 September 2024 with about 128 participants; Johor issued a cessation-of-business notice on 17 July 2026 for licensing breaches; claims about Israeli nationals unverified; Srinivasan put RM500M expansion on hold and said over RM100M invested without government funding; MoU with Kazakhstan signed by Deputy PM Zhaslan Madiyev, announced 22 July 2026

entries.topic: Próspera v. Honduras: charter, governance, community, repeal, court ruling, ICSID ARB/23/2

claims.text: Charter dated 23 August 2018; incorporation effective 29 December 2017; nine-member Próspera Council; residents select four trustees and the Promoter and Organizer (Honduras Próspera LLC, Delaware) selects four; resolutions and prior approval of statutes need two-thirds of the whole Council; amendments need two-thirds then CAMP approval within 45 days; resident referendum on rules only above 10,000 residents; e-residents cannot vote; GSP contract up to 50 years; expropriation requires compensation of 200% of the greater of market value or loss; Próspera Court subject to binding arbitration

Council of nine with four appointed by Honduras Próspera Inc. and a two-thirds threshold that gives the company an effective veto (NACLA via Wikipedia); about 2,000 residents in 2024; Committee for the Adoption of Best Practices appointed by the Honduran government approves rules; Honduran criminal law applies; construction began 2021; Brimen applied 2017

On 19 September 2020 Próspera rejected accusations of any intent or authority to expropriate land; its council resolved the project would never benefit from expropriation; first development 58 acres, 'far' from Crawfish Rock

Crawfish Rock residents (Luisa Connor: 'They deceived us big time'; 'We didn't even know what a Zede was') feared expropriation after expansion drawings appeared to include the community's centre; Próspera said it informed the community in June 2019 (resolution signed by 49 residents) and promised not to expropriate
Connor: 'The city will grow like a tumor'; Venessa Cárdenas: residents not consulted; claim ~$10.8bn; 32 members of Congress wrote to Biden that corporations had 'weaponized' ISDS
Honduran Congress repealed the ZEDE law unanimously on 21 April 2022

Supreme Court ruling signed 20 September 2024 by 15 magistrates annulled the ZEDE framework from its inception (articles 294, 303, 304, 329 reforms, ZEDE law, guarantees); ZEDE law passed 12 June 2013 by 102-26; 2022 repeal's constitutional amendment never ratified so ZEDEs operated legally; three ZEDEs; Castro: 'patriotic, historic, fair, and legal'; Ciudad Morazán called the ruling 'abusive'

Castro: ruling means not 'selling off our territory piecemeal or privatizing our sovereignty'; court said existing ZEDEs' fate to be addressed in addendum; Próspera warned of insecurity for investors and employees
Próspera statement 19 September 2024: 'There is nothing to gain from such a ruling'; a retroactive ruling would 'have no legitimacy' and strengthen expropriation claims

Claim up to US$10.775bn under CAFTA-DR seeking to honour a 50-year legal stability guarantee; Minister Pedro Barquero said government would defend itself and could not pay without diverting development funds (23 Dec 2022); ICSID registered the case, Brimen said Honduras unwilling to settle (Feb 2023)

ARB/23/2: request 19 Dec 2022; tribunal constituted 29 Jan 2024 (Fernández-Armesto, Vinuesa, Rivkin); Honduras challenge 19 Feb 2024 rejected, resumed 7 Aug 2024; 10.20.5 objection rejected 26 Feb 2025; Memorial 15 Oct 2025; remedy sought: restitution or US$1.630bn; six objections incl. essential security; bifurcation denied 19 March 2026

Claim cut from US$10.775bn to US$1.63bn (about 85%); the PGR attributed it to the state's defence, called the arbitration 'injusto e improcedente' and the original figures 'especulaciones sin sustento jurídico'
Honduras's ICSID denunciation received 24 Feb 2024, effective 25 Aug 2024; ratification deposited 17 July 2026; in force 16 Aug 2026; 159th Contracting State
Asfura re-signed ICSID 6 March 2026; Honduras faces 14 pending ICSID cases (Aug 2026); Próspera's Jorge Colindres hopes for conciliation; says ruling cost 1,500 jobs, 974 jobs in ZEDE by March 2026
85 economists (Progressive International letter, 19 March 2024) commended Honduras's ICSID withdrawal as a 'critical defense of Honduran democracy'; claim ~a third of GDP
Coinbase Ventures made a 'strategic investment' announced 21 January 2025, with North Island Ventures and BoostVC; amount undisclosed

NYT (30 Aug 2024) reported US$120 million raised including from venture funds backed by Thiel, Altman, Andreessen; Patri Friedman: in 2018 he created Pronomos 'with financing from Peter Thiel' when Próspera was about to be approved; fund invested in Próspera

Rep. Horsford (D-NV) on 12 January 2024 urged visa denials for Honduran officials advocating expropriation of US investments and cited Próspera's $100M+ and a '50-year legal stability guarantee'; Brimen donated $5,000 to Horsford in 2023 (Bloomberg via Wikipedia)

Próspera welcomed Rep. Gosar's Protect U.S. Investments Act (Jan 2023) to extend sanctions incl. visa denials for expropriation; Brimen: 'there needs to be more serious consequences for expropriation'

entries.topic: Argentina and exit projects; Trump's Freedom Cities pledge and its status

claims.text: Milei, as a candidate, visited +Colonia on 30 August 2023, met founder Eduardo Bastitta, and toured the site; project 500 hectares, $500M five-year plan; still awaiting final permits
Decree 524/2025 (Boletín Oficial 31 July 2025) created citizenship by investment via an agency under the Ministry of Economy; not operational as of January 2026; no Thiel link in the report
A Mises Wire essay (2024) argued Argentina needs 'ciudades libres' and attributed no proposal to the Milei government

An academic review of Milei's urban and housing policy (DNU 70/2023, rent deregulation, Ley 27.743, DNU 1017/2024) describes a 'ciudad libertaria' as an analytical model; no charter city, free city or special zone project is cited

Trump's campaign video (released 3 March 2023) called for a 'quantum leap in the American standard of living' and up to ten 'freedom cities' that 'will reopen the American frontier', on 0.5% of federal land chartered through a contest

PolitiFact rated the Freedom Cities promise 'Stalled' on 10 February 2026: no bill mentioning freedom cities on Congress.gov, no executive order, no Trump mention since 2023 per FactBase; Frontier Foundation: 'Drafts are circulating. This promise will be fulfilled.'; White House did not respond

The Freedom Cities Coalition, a project of NeWay Capital (central to Próspera's development), was drafting legislation; Próspera chief of staff Trey Goff said representatives had met the Trump administration, which was 'very receptive'

Bloomberg Law: large transfers of BLM land require an act of Congress; Tom Bell's draft would exempt freedom cities from the tax code, Clean Water Act, Endangered Species Act and labour law under the Property Clause; Andrew Mergen: Congress has broad authority but 'This would be at a whole other scale'; BLM's acting director had seen no specific proposal; White House no comment; Burgum on 17 March proposed selling up to 625 sq mi near cities for housing

AEI's 'Homesteading 2.0' (April 2025) proposed selling 850 sq mi of BLM land, 600 for about 20 Freedom Cities; Paul Dans called Freedom Cities part of a 'construction phase' after 'demolition' of the administrative state (NBC, 29 April 2025); Bell's draft would bar residents from voting in state elections
Sen. Mike Lee withdrew his provision to sell 0.25-0.5% of BLM land in 11 states from the reconciliation bill on 28 June 2025 after a parliamentarian ruling and House Republican opposition
Frontier Foundation, AEI and Charter Cities Institute pushed for first sites to be unveiled on 4 July 2026; FLPMA (1976) ended private sales of public land in practice
As of late July 2026 no law mentioned Freedom Cities (taz)
